Roofing in North Richland Hills, Texas

North Richland Hills spells out what happens when old shingles come off, from layer limits to new underlayment. One free number, answered any hour, connects you with an independent roofer that takes NRH calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 NRH tear-off rules
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. North Richland Hills

December 13, 2022, along Sayers Lane

Roofing in North Richland Hills, TX got a hard lesson before sunrise on a Tuesday in December 2022. A tornado crossed the city that morning, and the National Weather Service later rated it EF-1, with peak winds near 90 mph and a damage path of about a mile and a half.

News reports put its start near Sayers Lane just west of Davis Boulevard. North Richland Hills police described the damage running from around Smithfield and Starnes roads northeast toward Precinct Line and North Tarrant Parkway, and said about 20 homes and businesses were hit. It was one of many tornadoes counted across North Texas that morning.

An EF-1 does not flatten neighborhoods, but it peels shingles, lifts ridge caps and drops limbs, and a roof that looks fine from the driveway can leak for months afterward. That is the kind of call this line takes. DFW Expert Roofers is a free number, not a roofer. The automated assistant listens, then connects you with an independent, locally owned roofing company that works in NRH.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

What North Richland Hills expects when the old roof comes off

The city's Building Inspections FAQ goes further than most about the work itself. These are the points a homeowner can hold a roofer to.

  1. A registered contractor. Anyone doing work that needs permits and inspections must be registered with the city through the NRH E-Portal. Owners whose home carries a homestead exemption with the appraisal district may do their own work; every other roofing permit goes only to a registered contractor.
  2. A permit when decking is involved. The current FAQ says replacing shingles alone on a one or two family home needs no permit, while a re-roof that repairs or replaces decking does. Because an older FAQ said otherwise, confirm with the city.
  3. Two layers means a full tear-off. A roof carrying two or more layers of shingles must be stripped completely before new shingles go on.
  4. New underlayment. The underlayment must be replaced whenever the roof is re-shingled.
  5. Surprises get reported. If damaged decking or rafters appear after tear-off, the contractor must contact the city to modify the permit, and the field inspector has the final say.

Reading an NRH roofing quote

Because the city ties so much to decking and layers, a good quote here answers four things in writing. How many layers are on the roof today. What underlayment goes on. What one sheet of replacement decking costs if bad wood is found. And who will update the permit if that happens.

If a quote is silent on any of those, ask before you sign. A roofer who already works in North Richland Hills should not be surprised by the question, and the answers make it much easier to compare two bids line by line.

Insurance work adds one more rule that applies everywhere in Texas: the deductible is yours, and no roofer may absorb it.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

Four reasons NRH homeowners call

Wind damage that hides

The 2022 EF-1 path crossed streets full of homes. Lifted shingles can reseal crooked and leak later, so a closer look after any strong wind is worth asking for.

Old layers under new shingles

A house that was re-roofed over the original shingles years ago has two layers, and the city says both must come off. That changes the price and the schedule.

Shops and offices on the main roads

Every commercial re-roof in the city needs a permit, and insulation that comes off generally goes back to today's energy code. Business owners call to talk that through.

A phone that is always answered

The assistant answers at night and on weekends. When the roofer cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, need and urgency for a call back.

Questions for a roofer working in North Richland Hills

  • What business name is your NRH registration under, and does it match this contract?
  • How many layers of shingles are on my roof right now, and will you strip all of them?
  • Which underlayment are you putting down, by product name?
  • If you find soft decking, how will you show it to me, and will you update the city permit?
  • For a commercial roof: what insulation goes back on, and is it listed as its own line?
  • How do I get a copy of your liability insurance certificate from your agent?

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Unsure whether a North Richland Hills permit applies, or whether the wind did enough damage to matter? Call and describe it. The roofer you reach looks in person and writes up its own estimate.

Roofing questions from North Richland Hills

Do roofing companies in North Richland Hills TX have to register with the city?

Yes. The city's building FAQ says every contractor doing work that needs permits and inspections must be registered with North Richland Hills, and registration is done online through the NRH E-Portal. The city lists no fee for it, so there is no cost excuse for skipping it. Before you sign, ask the roofer for the exact business name it registered under and check that name against the contract.

Is a permit required to re-roof a house in North Richland Hills?

The city's current FAQ says one and two family homes do not need a permit when only shingles are replaced, but a re-roof that repairs or replaces decking does. An older version of the same FAQ said nearly every re-roof needed one, so call Building Inspections to confirm before work begins. Even without a permit, the city says the roof still has to meet Chapter 9 of the International Residential Code.

What if my NRH roofer finds rotten decking halfway through?

North Richland Hills expects the permit to be updated. Its FAQ tells contractors to contact the city and modify the permit when damaged decking or rafters show up after tear-off, and all work is subject to the field inspector's approval. Ask your roofer up front how it prices extra sheets and how it will show you the damage. Our roof replacement page explains the rest of a tear-off.

Does a business roof in North Richland Hills need a permit?

Yes. The city says every commercial building needs a building permit to re-roof, and that roof insulation taken off generally has to be replaced to meet the current energy code. That can change the scope and the price on a flat or low-slope roof, so ask the roofer to list insulation separately. See the commercial roofing page for more.

Who answers when I call about a roof in North Richland Hills?

First an automated assistant, which asks whether the call is about a roof and what went wrong with it. It then transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes NRH calls. DFW Expert Roofers never inspects or works on roofs and never charges you; the roofer you are connected with sets its own price. Roofing companies may pay the line for referrals.

Roof damage in North Richland Hills? Call the free line

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
